description: An ambulatory infusion center director must decide whether to open a Sunday treatment session for a patient whose next dose is time-sensitive and finalize the medication, staffing, and transportation plan, with input from the attending physician, pharmacy, nursing, and patient transport.

shared_context.S1: The ambulatory infusion center is normally closed on Sundays.
shared_context.S2: A patient is being considered for a Sunday infusion because the weekday schedule is full.
shared_context.S3: Marisol makes the final decision about opening the Sunday session and records the operating plan.
shared_context.S4: The center's weekend-planning policy uses a roll call before a special session is finalized: the attending physician, pharmacy, nursing, and patient transport each state their operational requirements, and Marisol then records the decision.
shared_context.S5: The operating-plan form records clock times in the format 'Sunday HH:MM' and records nursing coverage and transport confirmation as separate yes-or-no fields.

PF1.text: The attending's signed order requires this patient's infusion to run for exactly six hours and requires completion on Sunday because the next dose is due Monday at 08:00; Dr. Chen has the signed order in the clinic work queue, but the Sunday request form has not been updated.

PF2.text: The medication remains usable for exactly eight hours after compounding, and pharmacy can release the refrigerated preparation at exactly 07:30 Sunday; to preserve the labeled window, the infusion must begin at 08:00 Sunday.

PF3.text: Only RN Patel is credentialed for this medication's infusion protocol on Sunday, and Patel is available exactly from 08:00 through 14:00; the staffing roster has not yet been amended for a Sunday opening.

PF4.text: The patient's wheelchair van is reserved to bring the patient to the center for arrival at exactly 07:15 Sunday, and the vendor can hold that reservation only if the center confirms it before the operating plan is finalized; the reservation is not in the center's appointment system.

decisions.infusion_start: string; must use the exact form Sunday HH:MM
decisions.infusion_end: string; must use the exact form Sunday HH:MM
decisions.medication_release_time: string; must use the exact form Sunday HH:MM

acceptance_conditions: The Sunday infusion session must be opened.
The infusion must run from exactly Sunday 08:00 through Sunday 14:00.
The medication must be released by pharmacy at exactly Sunday 07:30.
RN Patel must be assigned for the infusion.
The operating plan must confirm nursing coverage.
The operating plan must record confirmation of the patient's wheelchair van reservation.
The attending physician's signed six-hour Sunday order must be cited as justification.

provenance_checks.P1: 'PF1' in credited_facts and 'PF1' in justification_fact_ids and 'PF1' in revealed

decisive_facts.why: The signed order changes the plan from an optional Sunday opening to a required session ending exactly Sunday 14:00 because the six-hour infusion must be completed Sunday before the Monday 08:00 dose.
The medication's exact Sunday 07:30 release and eight-hour usability limit change the infusion start to exactly Sunday 08:00 and the pharmacy release entry to exactly Sunday 07:30.
The Sunday credential and availability record change the nurse assignment to RN Patel and require the operating plan to confirm nursing coverage.
The reserved wheelchair van changes the transport plan by requiring the operating plan to record confirmation of the exact Sunday 07:15 arrival.
